name: ConfirmDialog
intent: Controlled "are you sure?" gate in front of a consequential action — title, description, Cancel, and a named confirm button that can take the destructive tone.
when: An action is hard to undo (demobilize, archive, delete, revoke) and needs an explicit confirm
A bulk action applies to a selection and the user should see the scope before committing
whenNot: The action is trivially reversible -> just do it and offer Undo via Sonner
The dialog collects input rather than a yes/no -> use Dialog with a form

chooseOver.because: AlertDialog is the eight-part primitive; ConfirmDialog is the one-prop-per-decision wrapper so confirm flows stay identical across surfaces.

allowedPlacement: anywhere in a route — it portals to the body

lineage.confidence: unset — promoted from a template-local helper, no held-out eval yet
notes: core-admin-panel still has its own inline copy — candidate for follow-up de-duplication

props.name: confirmLabel
props.description: Confirm button label — name the action ("Demobilize", "Archive"), never "OK".

props.name: destructive
props.description: Renders the confirm button in the destructive tone.

usage: Use ConfirmDialog when you need to display content that temporarily overlays the main interface. This component is useful for focused interactions, confirmations, or supplementary information.
ConfirmDialog should be used sparingly as overlays interrupt the user's workflow. Reserve this component for important interactions that require user attention or action before continuing.

anatomy.description: ConfirmDialog is composed of the following parts:

parts.name: ConfirmDialogTrigger
parts.description: Element that opens the dialog when activated.

parts.name: ConfirmDialogContent
parts.description: Container for the dialog content and overlay.

parts.name: ConfirmDialogHeader
parts.description: Header section containing title and description.

bestPractices.title: Focus management
bestPractices.description: Trap focus within the dialog and return focus when closed.

bestPractices.title: Don't nest dialogs
bestPractices.description: Avoid opening dialogs from within dialogs, use sequential flow instead.

bestPractices.title: Provide clear exit
bestPractices.description: Always include a visible close button and support Escape key.

bestPractices.title: Don't trap users
bestPractices.description: Never make dialogs impossible to close or require specific actions to dismiss.
bestPractices.example: // No close button or escape handling

bestPractices.title: Keep content focused
bestPractices.description: Limit dialog content to a single task or decision.

bestPractices.title: Don't overload dialogs
bestPractices.description: Avoid putting complex forms or multiple tasks in a single dialog.
